questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Morphology and modifications of flowering plants
questions.question: Which of the following is an underground stem modified for food storage?

solution.key_concept: Underground stems bear nodes and buds. Storage roots do not.
steps: Ginger is a rhizome, which is an underground stem with nodes and buds.
Carrot (conical) and turnip (napiform) are tap roots modified for storage.
Sweet potato is a tuberous adventitious root.
solution.why_not_others: Carrot, sweet potato and turnip are all modified roots, not stems.
solution.common_trap: Assuming every underground food-storing organ is a root.
solution.time_saving_tip: Look for nodes and buds. If an organ has them, it is a stem.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Morphology and modifications of flowering plants
questions.question: Which of the following pairs of plant and type of subaerial stem is correctly matched?

solution.key_concept: Subaerial stem modifications and their examples.
steps: Runners occur in grass and strawberry.
Stolons occur in mint and jasmine.
Offsets occur in Pistia and Eichhornia.
Suckers occur in banana, pineapple and Chrysanthemum.
solution.why_not_others: Mint has a stolon, strawberry has a runner and banana has a sucker.
solution.common_trap: Interchanging the examples of runner and stolon.
solution.time_saving_tip: Pair the aquatic plants Pistia and Eichhornia with offset.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Morphology and modifications of flowering plants
questions.question: A flattened petiole that functions like a leaf, called a phyllode, is found in

solution.key_concept: A phyllode is a leaf modification in which the petiole becomes flattened.
steps: Australian Acacia has a phyllode, which is a flattened petiole.
Opuntia has a phylloclade, which is a flattened stem.
Euphorbia has a fleshy cylindrical photosynthetic stem.
In pea, leaves are modified into tendrils.
solution.why_not_others: Opuntia and Euphorbia have modified stems, not modified petioles. Pea shows leaf tendrils.
solution.common_trap: Confusing phyllode (a modified petiole) with phylloclade (a modified stem).

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Morphology and modifications of flowering plants
questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: In pea, part of the leaf is modified into tendrils for climbing.
statements.R: In cucumber and pumpkin, tendrils develop from axillary buds.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: Tendrils can be modified leaves or modified stems.
steps: Pea has leaf tendrils, so A is true.
Cucumber and pumpkin have stem tendrils arising from axillary buds, so R is true.
R describes stem tendrils in other plants. It does not explain the leaf tendrils of pea.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
solution.why_not_others: R cannot explain A because it concerns a different organ in different plants. Both statements are true, so options 3 and 4 are wrong.
solution.common_trap: Thinking all tendrils arise from axillary buds.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Morphology and modifications of flowering plants
questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: Turnip is a napiform tap root, while sweet potato is a tuberous adventitious root.
statements.II: Colocasia and zaminkand store food in corms, which are underground stems.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: Storage roots versus storage stems.
steps: Turnip is a napiform tap root and sweet potato is a tuberous adventitious root, so Statement I is correct.
Colocasia and zaminkand have corms, which are underground stems, so Statement II is correct.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
solution.why_not_others: Both statements match the facts, so any option calling either statement incorrect is wrong.
solution.common_trap: Calling sweet potato a tap root, or treating Colocasia as a root.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Plant tissues
questions.question: Which of the following is the only living element of xylem?

solution.key_concept: Xylem is a complex tissue with four elements.
steps: Tracheids, vessels and xylem fibres are dead.
Xylem parenchyma is the only living xylem element.
solution.why_not_others: The other three are dead elements.
solution.common_trap: Assuming vessels are living because they conduct water.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Plant tissues
questions.question: Which simple permanent tissue has walls thickened at the corners, gives mechanical support to young dicot stems and petioles, and is absent in monocots?

solution.key_concept: Features of simple permanent tissues.
steps: Collenchyma has corner thickenings of cellulose, hemicellulose and pectin.
It supports young dicot stems and petioles and is absent in monocots.
solution.why_not_others: Parenchyma is thin-walled. Sclerenchyma is dead and lignified. Xylem fibres belong to a complex tissue.
solution.common_trap: Choosing sclerenchyma just because the question mentions mechanical support.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Plant tissues
questions.question: In gymnosperms, the cells that take the place of companion cells are

solution.key_concept: Phloem in gymnosperms differs from phloem in angiosperms.
steps: Gymnosperms have sieve cells instead of sieve tubes.
Gymnosperms have albuminous cells instead of companion cells.
solution.why_not_others: Sieve cells replace sieve tubes, not companion cells. Phloem parenchyma is a separate element. Tracheids are xylem cells.
solution.common_trap: Swapping sieve cells and albuminous cells.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Plant tissues
questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

list_II.label: II
list_II.text: Primary growth in length at root and shoot tips

solution.key_concept: Types of meristem and the nature of sclerenchyma.
steps: Apical meristem causes primary growth in length at the tips (A-II).
Intercalary meristem lies at the base of internodes in grasses (B-III).
Lateral meristems, the vascular and cork cambium, cause growth in girth (C-IV).
Sclerenchyma consists of dead, lignified cells (D-I).
solution.why_not_others: Each of the other options mismatches at least two pairs.
solution.common_trap: Linking intercalary meristem with growth at the tips.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Plant tissues
questions.question: Which of the following statements about plant tissues are correct?

statements.A: Xylem is exarch in roots, with protoxylem towards the periphery.
statements.B: Mature sieve tube elements have a prominent nucleus.
statements.C: Phloem fibres are the only dead cells of phloem.
statements.D: Guard cells are dumb-bell shaped in grasses.

solution.key_concept: Features of xylem, phloem and the epidermal tissue system.
steps: A is true: root xylem is exarch.
B is false: mature sieve tube elements lack a nucleus.
C is true: phloem (bast) fibres are the only dead phloem cells.
D is true: guard cells of grasses are dumb-bell shaped.
E is false: root hairs are unicellular.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): A, C and D only
solution.why_not_others: The other options include B or E, which are false.
solution.common_trap: Mixing up unicellular root hairs with multicellular stem trichomes.
solution.time_saving_tip: Once B and E are ruled out, only option (2) remains.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Anatomy and functions of root, stem and leaf
questions.question: The Casparian strips present in the endodermal cells of roots are made of

solution.key_concept: The endodermis carries suberised Casparian strips.
steps: Casparian strips are deposits of suberin.
They block apoplastic water flow.
solution.why_not_others: Lignin is found in sclerenchyma. Cellulose and pectin thicken collenchyma walls.
solution.common_trap: Choosing lignin because it is the most familiar wall-thickening substance.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Anatomy and functions of root, stem and leaf
questions.question: A transverse section shows alternating xylem and phloem patches, more than six xylem bundles, a large well-developed pith and no secondary growth. The section is of a

solution.key_concept: Polyarch radial bundles indicate a monocot root.
steps: Alternating xylem and phloem patches mean radial bundles, which indicates a root.
More than six xylem bundles (polyarch) together with a large pith indicate a monocot root.
solution.why_not_others: A dicot root has only 2 to 4 xylem patches and a small pith. Stems have conjoint bundles, not radial ones.
solution.common_trap: Assuming a large pith always means a dicot stem.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Anatomy and functions of root, stem and leaf
questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of a monocot stem?
options: Open vascular bundles arranged in a ring
Numerous scattered closed bundles, each enclosed in a sclerenchymatous bundle sheath
Ground tissue clearly differentiated into cortex and pith

solution.key_concept: Anatomy of the monocot stem.
steps: A monocot stem has numerous scattered, closed bundles.
Each bundle is enclosed in a sclerenchymatous bundle sheath and has a water-containing cavity.
Its ground tissue is not differentiated into cortex and pith.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): Numerous scattered closed bundles, each enclosed in a sclerenchymatous bundle sheath
solution.why_not_others: Options 1, 2 and 4 describe a dicot stem. The monocot stem has a sclerenchymatous hypodermis.
solution.common_trap: Thinking monocot stem bundles are open.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Anatomy and functions of root, stem and leaf
questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: Grass leaves roll up during water stress, which reduces water loss.
statements.R: Bulliform cells present on the abaxial epidermis become fully turgid during water stress.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: Bulliform cells in grass leaves.
steps: Grass leaves do roll in water stress to cut water loss, so A is true.
Bulliform cells lie on the adaxial epidermis, not the abaxial one.
During water stress they lose turgor rather than becoming turgid, so R is false.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): A is true but R is false
solution.why_not_others: R is false on two counts, its location and its turgor state, so options 1, 2 and 4 are wrong.
solution.common_trap: Thinking that turgid bulliform cells cause the leaf to roll.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Anatomy and functions of root, stem and leaf
questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: In a dorsiventral leaf, palisade mesophyll lies towards the adaxial side and more stomata occur on the abaxial surface.
statements.II: In the vascular bundles of a leaf, phloem lies towards the adaxial side and xylem towards the abaxial side.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: Anatomy of the dicot leaf.
steps: Palisade mesophyll is adaxial and stomata are more numerous on the abaxial surface, so Statement I is correct.
In leaf bundles, xylem is adaxial and phloem is abaxial, so Statement II has them reversed and is incorrect.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
solution.why_not_others: Statement II reverses the positions of xylem and phloem. Statement I is accurate.
solution.common_trap: Reversing the positions of xylem and phloem in a leaf.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Inflorescence: cymose and racemose
questions.question: In a racemose inflorescence, the flowers are arranged in
options: Basipetal succession, with the oldest flower at the apex
Acropetal succession, with the oldest flower at the apex
Basipetal succession, with the oldest flower at the base
Acropetal succession, with the oldest flower at the base

solution.key_concept: In racemose inflorescence, the main axis grows indefinitely.
steps: Because the main axis keeps growing, new flowers form towards the apex.
This gives acropetal order, with the oldest flower at the base.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): Acropetal succession, with the oldest flower at the base
solution.why_not_others: Option 1 describes a cymose inflorescence. Options 2 and 3 are internally inconsistent.
solution.common_trap: Placing the oldest racemose flower at the top.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Inflorescence: cymose and racemose
questions.question: A catkin, which is a pendulous spike of unisexual flowers, is found in

solution.key_concept: Types of racemose inflorescence and their examples.
steps: Mulberry bears a catkin.
Achyranthes has a spike, coriander an umbel and mustard a raceme.
solution.why_not_others: Each of the other plants has a different racemose type.
solution.common_trap: Choosing Achyranthes because a catkin is a kind of spike.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Inflorescence: cymose and racemose
questions.question: A cymose inflorescence in which two lateral branches arise below the terminal flower is seen in

solution.key_concept: Cymes are classified by the number of lateral branches below the terminal flower.
steps: Two lateral branches means a dichasial cyme.
Jasmine has a dichasial cyme.
solution.why_not_others: Calotropis has a polychasial cyme. Sunflower (capitulum) and candytuft (corymb) are racemose.
solution.common_trap: Choosing Calotropis, which is polychasial.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Inflorescence: cymose and racemose
questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

solution.key_concept: Examples of racemose inflorescence types.
steps: Spadix: banana (A-III).
Umbel: coriander (B-I).
Corymb: candytuft (C-IV).
Capitulum: Tridax (D-II).
solution.why_not_others: The other options swap spadix with umbel or corymb with capitulum.
solution.common_trap: Matching corymb with Tridax because in both the flowers reach one level.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Inflorescence: cymose and racemose
questions.question: Which of the following statements about inflorescences are correct?

statements.A: In a cymose inflorescence, the main axis terminates in a flower.
statements.B: In a capitulum, the oldest florets lie at the centre.
statements.C: Monochasial cymes may be helicoid or scorpioid.
statements.D: A spike bears sessile flowers, as in Achyranthes.
statements.E: Cymes are classified by the total number of flowers on the floral axis.

options: A, C, D and E only

solution.key_concept: Distinguishing cymose from racemose inflorescence.
steps: A is true: in a cyme the main axis ends in a flower.
B is false: a capitulum is racemose, so the oldest florets are at the periphery.
C is true: monochasial cymes are helicoid or scorpioid.
D is true: a spike has sessile flowers, as in Achyranthes.
E is false: cymes are classified by the number of lateral branches below the terminal flower.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): A, C and D only
solution.why_not_others: Options 1, 3 and 4 each include B or E, which are false.
solution.common_trap: Applying the cymose rule (oldest flower at the centre) to the capitulum.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Flower, fruit and seed
questions.question: Twisted aestivation of the corolla is seen in:

solution.key_concept: Aestivation is the arrangement of sepals or petals in the bud. It may be valvate, twisted, imbricate or vexillary.
steps: Twisted aestivation occurs in China rose, lady's finger and cotton.
Calotropis is valvate, Cassia is imbricate and pea is vexillary.
solution.why_not_others: Calotropis shows valvate aestivation, Cassia shows imbricate aestivation and pea shows vexillary aestivation.
solution.common_trap: Confusing imbricate (Cassia, gulmohur) with twisted aestivation.
solution.time_saving_tip: Remember the twisted trio of Malvaceae: China rose, lady's finger and cotton.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Flower, fruit and seed
questions.question: Which of the following plants bears perigynous flowers with a half-inferior ovary?

solution.key_concept: By ovary position, flowers are hypogynous (superior ovary), perigynous (half-inferior ovary) or epigynous (inferior ovary).
steps: Perigynous flowers are found in plum, rose and peach.
Mustard and brinjal are hypogynous, and guava is epigynous.
solution.why_not_others: Mustard and brinjal have a superior ovary (hypogynous), while guava has an inferior ovary (epigynous).
solution.common_trap: Assuming every fleshy fruit, such as guava, comes from a perigynous flower.
solution.time_saving_tip: For perigynous, recall the rose-family trio: plum, rose and peach.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Flower, fruit and seed
questions.question: In a maize grain, the single cotyledon is represented by the:

solution.key_concept: The maize seed is a monocot seed. It is usually endospermic and has an aleurone layer, a scutellum, a coleoptile and a coleorhiza.
steps: The scutellum is the single cotyledon of maize.
The coleoptile sheathes the plumule, and the coleorhiza sheathes the radicle.
The aleurone layer belongs to the endosperm region.
solution.why_not_others: The coleoptile covers the plumule, the coleorhiza covers the radicle and the aleurone layer is part of the endosperm region. None of these is the cotyledon.
solution.common_trap: Mixing up coleoptile (plumule sheath) and coleorhiza (radicle sheath) with the cotyledon.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Flower, fruit and seed
questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: Coconut is a drupe in which the edible part is the fleshy mesocarp.
statements.R: A drupe develops from a monocarpellary superior ovary and is one-seeded.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: Drupes such as mango and coconut differ in the nature of their mesocarp.
steps: In coconut, the mesocarp is fibrous, not fleshy. The fleshy edible mesocarp describes mango, so A is false.
A drupe does develop from a monocarpellary superior ovary and is one-seeded, so R is true.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): A is false but R is true
solution.why_not_others: A is false, so any option that treats A as true is ruled out.
solution.common_trap: Carrying the mango fact (fleshy edible mesocarp) over to coconut.
solution.time_saving_tip: Mango has a fleshy mesocarp; coconut has a fibrous mesocarp.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Flower, fruit and seed
questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: Castor is an endospermic dicot seed, whereas bean, gram and pea are non-endospermic dicot seeds.
statements.II: In Dianthus and Primrose, the ovules are borne on the inner wall of the ovary, which is parietal placentation.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: Dicot seeds may be endospermic or non-endospermic. Placentation types must be matched with the correct examples.
steps: Castor is an endospermic dicot seed, while bean, gram and pea are non-endospermic, so Statement I is correct.
Dianthus and Primrose show free central placentation, with ovules on a central axis and no septa, so Statement II is incorrect.
Parietal placentation is seen in mustard and Argemone.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
solution.why_not_others: Statement II describes parietal placentation, which belongs to mustard and Argemone, not to Dianthus and Primrose.
solution.common_trap: Mixing up parietal and free central placentation.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Families: Malvaceae, Cruciferae, Leguminosae, Compositae and Gramineae
questions.question: The characteristic fruit of the family Cruciferae is a:

solution.key_concept: Each family has a characteristic fruit type.
steps: Cruciferae bears a siliqua (or silicula).
Compositae bears a cypsela, Gramineae a caryopsis and Leguminosae a legume.
solution.why_not_others: Cypsela belongs to Compositae, caryopsis to Gramineae and legume to Leguminosae.
solution.common_trap: Interchanging cypsela and caryopsis.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Families: Malvaceae, Cruciferae, Leguminosae, Compositae and Gramineae
questions.question: Stamens with fused anthers but free filaments are characteristic of:

solution.key_concept: Syngenesious stamens have fused anthers and free filaments.
steps: Syngenesious, epipetalous stamens are typical of Compositae.
Malvaceae has monadelphous stamens, pea has diadelphous stamens and mustard has tetradynamous stamens.
solution.why_not_others: In Malvaceae the filaments, not the anthers, are fused into one bundle. Pea has (9)+1 diadelphous stamens. Mustard has tetradynamous stamens.
solution.common_trap: Confusing syngenesious stamens (anthers fused) with monadelphous stamens (filaments fused).

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Families: Malvaceae, Cruciferae, Leguminosae, Compositae and Gramineae
questions.question: Which interpretation of the floral formula $\%\ K_{(5)}\ C_{1+2+(2)}\ A_{(9)+1}\ \underline{G}_{1}$ is correct?
options: The ovary is inferior and monocarpellary
All five petals are free, and the stamens are monadelphous
The flower is actinomorphic, with diadelphous stamens
The two keel petals are fused, the stamens are diadelphous, and the ovary is superior

solution.key_concept: This is the Papilionoideae (pea) floral formula. Brackets mean fusion, and a line below G means a superior ovary.
steps: $\%$ means the flower is zygomorphic.
$C_{1+2+(2)}$ means 1 standard, 2 wings and 2 fused keel petals.
$A_{(9)+1}$ means diadelphous stamens.
$\underline{G}_{1}$ means a superior monocarpellary ovary.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): The two keel petals are fused, the stamens are diadelphous, and the ovary is superior
solution.why_not_others: A line below G means superior, not inferior. The keel petals are fused, so not all petals are free, and (9)+1 is diadelphous, not monadelphous. The $\%$ symbol means zygomorphic, not actinomorphic.
solution.common_trap: Reading the line below G as an inferior ovary.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Families: Malvaceae, Cruciferae, Leguminosae, Compositae and Gramineae
questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

solution.key_concept: Diagnostic features identify families.
steps: Epicalyx is a feature of Malvaceae (A-III).
A replum with parietal placentation is a feature of Cruciferae (B-IV).
A calyx reduced to pappus is a feature of Compositae (C-II).
A perianth reduced to lodicules is a feature of Gramineae (D-I).
solution.why_not_others: Each of the other options misplaces at least one pair, such as giving pappus to Gramineae or epicalyx to Cruciferae.
solution.common_trap: Linking pappus and lodicules to the wrong family, since both are reduced floral parts.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Families: Malvaceae, Cruciferae, Leguminosae, Compositae and Gramineae
questions.question: Which of the following statements about angiosperm families are correct?

statements.A: In Cruciferae, the two short stamens are outer and the four long stamens are inner.
statements.B: In Malvaceae, the anthers are dithecous.
statements.C: In Compositae, the ray florets are ligulate, zygomorphic and often female or neuter.
statements.D: In Gramineae, the fruit is a caryopsis in which the pericarp is fused with the seed coat.
statements.E: Mimosoideae has zygomorphic flowers with imbricate aestivation.

solution.key_concept: This tests family-specific floral details.
steps: A is true: tetradynamous stamens are 2 short outer and 4 long inner.
B is false: Malvaceae anthers are monothecous (reniform).
C is true: ray florets are ligulate, zygomorphic and often female or neuter.
D is true: the caryopsis has its pericarp fused with the seed coat.
E is false: Mimosoideae flowers are actinomorphic with valvate aestivation. Zygomorphic flowers with imbricate aestivation describe Caesalpinioideae.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): A, C and D only
solution.why_not_others: Any option containing B or E is wrong, because Malvaceae anthers are monothecous and Mimosoideae flowers are actinomorphic and valvate.
solution.common_trap: Swapping the features of Mimosoideae and Caesalpinioideae.
solution.time_saving_tip: Eliminate options containing B or E first.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Animal tissues
questions.question: The inner lining of the bronchioles and fallopian tubes is formed by:

solution.key_concept: Each type of simple epithelium has characteristic locations.
steps: Ciliated epithelium lines the bronchioles and fallopian tubes.
Squamous epithelium lines alveoli and blood vessels, and cuboidal epithelium lines nephron tubules.
solution.why_not_others: Squamous epithelium is found in alveoli and blood vessel walls, compound epithelium in skin and the buccal cavity, and cuboidal epithelium in gland ducts and nephrons.
solution.common_trap: Choosing squamous epithelium because the bronchioles are part of the lungs.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Animal tissues
questions.question: Which structure allows ions and small molecules to pass directly between adjacent animal cells?

solution.key_concept: Cell junctions perform different functions.
steps: Tight junctions stop leakage.
Adhering junctions cement neighbouring cells together.
Gap junctions allow passage of ions and small molecules.
solution.why_not_others: Tight junctions prevent leakage and adhering junctions only cement cells. A brush border is made of microvilli and is not a cell junction.
solution.common_trap: Thinking tight junctions permit exchange between cells.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Animal tissues
questions.question: Ligaments, which attach bone to bone, are an example of:

solution.key_concept: Dense connective tissue is either regular or irregular.
steps: Tendons and ligaments are dense regular connective tissue.
The dermis of the skin is dense irregular connective tissue.
solution.why_not_others: Dense irregular tissue is found in the dermis, areolar tissue is loose connective tissue and cartilage is specialised connective tissue.
solution.common_trap: Assigning ligaments to dense irregular tissue.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Animal tissues
questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: Cardiac muscle cells contract as a unit.
statements.R: Cardiac muscle cells are joined to one another by intercalated discs.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: Intercalated discs coordinate the contraction of cardiac muscle.
steps: Cardiac muscle cells are joined by intercalated discs, so R is true.
These discs let the cells contract as a unit, so A is true and R explains A.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
solution.why_not_others: Both statements are true and directly linked, so options (2), (3) and (4) do not fit.
solution.common_trap: Marking option (2) without recognising the cause-effect link.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Animal tissues
questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: Neuroglia make up less than one-half the volume of neural tissue.
statements.II: Goblet cells are unicellular glands, whereas salivary glands are multicellular glands.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: This tests the composition of neural tissue and the types of glandular epithelium.
steps: Neuroglia make up more than one-half the volume of neural tissue, so Statement I is incorrect.
Goblet cells are unicellular glands and salivary glands are multicellular, so Statement II is correct.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
solution.why_not_others: Statement I reverses the actual proportion of neuroglia, so any option calling it correct is wrong.
solution.common_trap: Assuming neurons must make up most of the volume of neural tissue.

questions.question: How many digits are present on each forelimb of a frog?

solution.key_concept: The forelimbs and hindlimbs of a frog differ in digit number.
steps: Each forelimb has 4 digits.
Each hindlimb has 5 webbed digits for swimming.
solution.why_not_others: 5 is the number of digits on the hindlimb, and 3 and 6 are incorrect.
solution.common_trap: Giving the hindlimb count (5) for the forelimb.

questions.question: In a male frog, the vasa efferentia that arise from the testes enter the kidney and open into the:

solution.key_concept: This tests the route of sperm in the male frog.
steps: 10 to 12 vasa efferentia enter the kidney.
They open into Bidder's canal, which then joins the urinogenital duct.
solution.why_not_others: The vasa efferentia reach the urinogenital duct only through Bidder's canal and do not open into the cloaca directly. The mesorchium is the fold that attaches the testes to the kidneys.
solution.common_trap: Skipping Bidder's canal and choosing the urinogenital duct.

questions.question: In the heart of a frog, the sinus venosus opens into the:

solution.key_concept: The frog heart has three chambers plus a sinus venosus and a conus arteriosus.
steps: The sinus venosus opens into the right atrium.
The conus arteriosus arises from the ventricle on the ventral side.
solution.why_not_others: The left atrium and ventricle do not receive the sinus venosus, and the conus arteriosus leaves the ventricle.
solution.common_trap: Confusing the sinus venosus with the conus arteriosus.

questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

solution.key_concept: Each sense in the frog has a specific sense organ.
steps: Touch is sensed by sensory papillae (A-III).
Taste is sensed by taste buds (B-IV).
Smell is sensed by the nasal epithelium (C-I).
Hearing is by the tympanum with internal ears (D-II).
solution.why_not_others: The other options swap touch with taste, smell with hearing, or touch with smell.
solution.common_trap: Assuming frogs hear through an external ear. They have only a tympanum and internal ears.

questions.subject: biology

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the frog are correct?

statements.B: The red blood cells of frogs are nucleated.
statements.C: The tongue is bilobed, attached posteriorly and free anteriorly.
statements.D: Males bear a copulatory pad on the first digit of each forelimb.
statements.E: The ovaries are connected to the kidneys through Bidder's canal.

options: A, B, C and D only

solution.key_concept: This tests excretion, blood, the digestive system and the reproductive system of the frog.
steps: A is true: frogs are ureotelic.
B is true: frog RBCs are nucleated.
C is false: the tongue is attached anteriorly and free posteriorly.
D is true: males have a copulatory pad on the first digit of each forelimb.
E is false: the ovaries have no functional connection with the kidneys, and Bidder's canal belongs to the male.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): A, B and D only
solution.why_not_others: Options containing C or E are wrong because the tongue attachment is reversed in C and the female has no kidney connection, as claimed in E.
solution.common_trap: Reversing the attachment of the tongue, or giving Bidder's canal to the female.
solution.time_saving_tip: Eliminate options containing C or E first.
